knowledge_units.context_summary: TbB4 exhibits multi-step metamagnetic behavior between 16 and 28 T when a magnetic field is applied along the c-axis, contrasting with the linear magnetization expected for XY-type magnets. The material crystallizes in a tetragonal structure with a Shastry-Sutherland lattice of rare-earth ions, where frustration plays a central role in its magnetic properties. The magnetic structure involves antiferromagnetic interactions J1, J2, and J3, with J2 bonds remaining unsatisfied in the high-temperature phase.

knowledge_units.context_summary: TbB4 exhibits a multi-step magnetization process with nine reported steps, where the one-half magnetization plateau is the most prominent feature. Resonant magnetic x-ray diffraction (RMXD) experiments were conducted on TbB4 single crystals using synchrotron x-rays at the Tb LIII absorption edge under pulsed magnetic fields up to 29 T. The experimental setup utilized a split-pair pulsed magnet and an avalanche photodiode detector to measure diffraction intensity with microsecond resolution.

knowledge_units.context_summary: Resonant magnetic x-ray diffraction experiments on TbB4 revealed that magnetization plateau phases retain significant magnetic intensity in the 100 reflection. Polarization analysis confirmed that this intensity originates from in-plane (ab-plane) magnetic moment components rather than the c-axis component. The persistence of these in-plane components indicates that the plateau phases possess a canted magnetic structure with large XY-type moment components.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The authors propose a spin model for TbB4 where plateau phases consist of coexisting hard XY-type and Ising-like magnetic moments. Calculations using this model reproduce the one-half magnetization plateau and suggest that frustration lifts state degeneracy to create multi-step metamagnetic transitions.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The text explains how magnetic frustration in TbB4 lifts degeneracy at critical fields to create multi-step magnetization plateaus. It contrasts the energy relaxation mechanisms of one-third and one-half plateau phases, noting that the former is frustrated while the latter is not. The authors conclude that frustration-driven successive metamagnetic transitions are a general mechanism in such systems.
